definitions.explanation: A test where answers are written on paper, as opposed to an oral or practical exam. Common in school entrance exams, certification tests, and employment screenings in Japan.

examples.japanese: {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}に{合格|ごうかく}した。
{面接|めんせつ}の{前|まえ}に{筆記試験|ひっきしけん}がある。
examples.english: There is a written exam before the interview.

examples.japanese: {運転免許|うんてんめんきょ}を{取|と}るには{筆記試験|ひっきしけん}と{実技試験|じつぎしけん}の{両方|りょうほう}に{受|う}からなければならない。
examples.english: To get a driver's license, you must pass both the written and practical exams.

notes: Common collocations: {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}を{受|う}ける (to take a written exam), {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}に{合格|ごうかく}する (to pass), {筆記試験|ひっきしけん}に{落|お}ちる (to fail). Contrasts with {面接|めんせつ} (interview), {口述試験|こうじゅつしけん} (oral exam), and {実技試験|じつぎしけん} (practical exam). In Japan, many hiring processes include a {筆記試験|ひっきしけん} covering general knowledge or aptitude (SPI test).
